subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
Given the low effort budget, I'm planning a compact but solid scene: a red panda perched on a mossy stone, done in Genshin-style toon shading with cel paints, fur edges, and anime-style eyes, built using the toon kit imports. I'm sketching out the base rock geometry before moving to the character itself.

The panda will stand quadruped on the stone with a ringed tail, so I'm working out the skeleton hierarchy -- a single root joint at the origin, hips as its child, then spine, neck, head, and jaw chains running forward while the tail chain extends backward, plus limb chains for all four legs rigged to foot positions resting on the stone's top surface.

For the coat I'm giving it a cel-shaded fur edge effect going from rust-red on the back to dark countershading on the belly, matching red panda coloring. For the head I'm building a scaled sphere for the skull, adding a small cream muzzle and black nose, round cream-rimmed ears, and starting on the cheek ruffs.

Writing face paint logic...

Then for the eyes I'll place anime-style iris decals on the skull surface, positioned near the head center with a slight angular offset, using green/amber coloring and small sizing, skipping separate tear marks since the eye shape already carries its own blush detail.

Now I'm working through the four-legged structure, building each leg as a three-point chain (shoulder, elbow, foot/hand) parented to spine joints for front legs and hips for hind legs, sweeping them with tapered dark-colored radii and adding dark scaled paw spheres at the feet, deciding to skip separate toe/claw details for simplicity.

I'm positioning the hind legs further back and lower, adjusting foot coordinates so the paw spheres sit right on top of the stone surface, with root and target points calculated so each leg's bend direction (forward for hind knees, backward for front elbows) looks natural.

For the tail, I'm building a curved catmull-rom chain from the hips sweeping upward then down, with varying radius along its length, applying rust-colored stripe texturing with a darker tip, and letting it hang out over the edge of the stone for visual balance.

I'm anchoring the tail start to the hips joint position so it parents correctly to the body chain, then shaping the body sweep itself with varying rib/belly radii and a rounded cap, applying a darker coat tone underneath via normal-based shading. For ears, I'm placing small scaled spheres at the head joint, oriented using the head's local forward-facing axes.

Adding ear tilt rotation...

Now for the nose and mouth — placing a small dark nose sphere at the muzzle front, a cream lower jaw sphere positioned below and forward on the head, with a jaw joint for articulation. Then I'm adding cheek ruffs using cone-shaped spikes radiating outward and downward from the sides of the head for a fluffy look.

Small cream brow dots go just above each eye, positioned carefully onto the head's curved surface using the ellipsoid geometry to get the right offset. For the stone base, I'm using a lathe shape with a procedural paint function that applies mossy green mottling to upward-facing surfaces and gray stone elsewhere.

Checking proportions: panda head height and stone base height line up fine, feet sit just above the stone top. For the tail, stripe coloring should be enough without a separate gradient for the tip. I'm deciding to skip extra flourishes like glowing sprites or seelie-like accents, and skip a scarf too — keeping the design focused on the named brief elements rather than adding unrequested embellishments.

Now I'm working out the limb and spine chain code, defining body color paints and sweep functions, and pinning down fixed joint coordinates for the head and neck so the pose stays anatomically consistent.

Continuing with the skull part as a scaled sphere, placing eye decals using angular offsets around the head center, and sizing the nose and eyes before finalizing the full build.
